statement: KEEP EXCLUDED as of 2026-07-18; do not put XDNA2 NPU on the primary product path.
Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 / Strix Halo maps to upstream npu5: PCI 1022:17f0 revision 0x11.
The current upstream driver recognizes 1022:17f0 revision 0x11 and declares both npu.sbin and npu_7.sbin firmware paths.
amdxdna Kconfig depends on AMD_IOMMU, DRM_ACCEL, PCI/HAS_IOMEM and X86_64.
The AIE2/npu5 initialization path rejects execution under a hypervisor.
The AIE2/npu5 initialization path rejects operation without an IOMMU group.
Opening an amdxdna client normally binds IOMMU SVA and obtains a PASID; absence of PASID fails unless a carveout path is configured.
The NPU is explicitly non-cache-coherent and requires explicit host-cache synchronization.
Data movement is described as DMA between host DDR and NPU memory-tile/L2 storage under ctrlcode orchestration.
The upstream device record exposes 16 hardware contexts for npu5.
Scheduling combines spatial partitioning and temporal sharing, with DRM scheduler machinery in the host driver and firmware enforcement on device.
The UAPI contains QoS, BO synchronization, firmware-version, telemetry, power and utilization query structures.
System suspend stops the NPU; resume reloads firmware and recreates/resumes contexts.
Suspend/resume should not be assumed transparent to an application until a workload survives repeated cycles on the target.
linux-firmware contains two 17f0_11 firmware tracks: npu.sbin.1.0.0.166 and npu.sbin.1.1.2.65 via npu_7.sbin.
The vendor legacy driver for npu5 expects npu.dev.sbin and declares minimum firmware 6.12.
AMD warns that driver/firmware mismatches commonly cause mailbox timeouts or aborted commands.
AMD warns that a newer XRT/plugin can issue ioctls missing from an older in-tree driver, including telemetry/array queries.
AMD's documented Linux 1.7.1 reference is Ubuntu 24.04, kernel >=6.10, Python 3.12.x, with exact account-downloaded XRT/plugin packages.
The actual target distro, kernel build, kernel config, firmware package and installed XRT/Ryzen AI package inventory are unknown.
Open low-level components exist: kernel driver, XRT, llvm-aie/Peano and mlir-aie/IRON.
The documented high-level ONNX/Vitis AI and OGA deployment flows rely on AMD's packaged runtime/compiler assets and EULA-governed downloads.
ONNX opset 17 is the recommended CNN/transformer interchange path; FP32 transformer inputs are compiled through BF16.
Documented data-type families include BF16, XINT8, A8W8 and A16W8, subject to model and operator constraints.
Operator-table support is broad rather than universal; specific configurations can remain unsupported.
Vitis AI EP may partition unsupported model subgraphs to CPU; useful NPU coverage must be measured from the actual assignment report.
No llama.cpp transformer/NPU offload path is established; AMD documents llama.cpp for iGPU.
AMD's Whisper.cpp NPU acceleration is currently Windows-only; Linux support is planned.
The Linux LLM path is documented as NPU-only and uses versioned AMD-prepared model/deployment assets.
Ryzen AI 1.7.1 lists NPU support for SmolLM and SmolLM2 135M instruction models.
The existence of a 135M OGA model does not establish a useful draft-model integration, speculative-decoding interface or target performance.
AMD publishes an exact DistilBERT sentiment classifier example using VitisAIExecutionProvider, ONNX opset 17, BF16, batch 1 and fixed length 128.
AMD publishes an NPU BGE embedding implementation, but the captured public RAG instructions are pinned to a 1.7.0 hybrid/Conda flow and do not establish Linux qualification.
No captured primary Linux reranker example or exact supported reranker model was found.
Moderation can be represented as a classifier workload, but the sentiment example does not establish moderation accuracy, labels or policy fitness.
No local latency, throughput, energy, memory, thermal, correctness or recovery measurement exists for the target.
The only permitted re-entry activity is an isolated classifier experiment after a read-only substrate probe; it must not modify the HIP/Vulkan path.
Hashes for account-gated AMD DEB/TGZ packages are not available in this research capture.
The public XRT/compiler repository HEADs are not proven to be the build inputs for AMD's 1.7.1 binary packages.
Firmware WHENCE marks the amdnpu payload redistributable and points to LICENSE.amdnpu; this bundle does not restate unreviewed license terms.
